references.text: Hosea refers directly to Jacob's struggle: he wrestled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and sought favor. This is the central prophetic commentary on the event in Gen 32:25.
Jacob receives the name Israel because he has struggled with God and humans and prevailed – the direct result of the wrestling match in verse 25.
Jacob names the place Peniel ('Face of God') because he saw God face to face and his life was spared. This identifies the mysterious opponent.
Those who wait on the Lord will renew their strength – a thematic parallel to Jacob's perseverance in the struggle throughout the night until dawn.
Jesus' parable about the widow who did not give up but kept praying – a parallel to Jacob's perseverance in prayer and struggle with God through the night.
Eph 6:12 on spiritual warfare – a New Testament reflection that the believer's struggle is not against flesh and blood, just as Jacob's struggle was also against a supernatural opponent.
